body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 58be8266565004db2bd42bb885468d0942540b6f -->
**Needs changes before merge.** There is one small request: the PR says an inverted Facing window is still refused when the op is created, but no test pins that. The fix and the posted output are correct.

### What looks good
- The root cause in #1409 is fixed at the source. `seed_facing` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs:1231-1240`) now seeds Top of Stock down to Top of Model. The MCP `seed_params` and the GUI `quick_params` both get these heights, and the UI pin checks that the two are equal.
- I read the `depth_sane` relaxation (`crates/app/src/operation/heights_sel.rs:176-183`) closely. It holds:
  - It is scoped to `OpParams::Facing` only. Other turning kinds still use the strict `t > b` arm, and the `must cut downward` pins in `turning_bore`, `turning_blade`, `turning_form`, `turning_contour` and `turning_thread` still pass.
  - NaN still refuses, because `t >= b` is false for NaN.
  - A level window cannot emit anything. `turning::facing` refuses it with `GenError::Empty` (`crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs:146`) before any move is built. That is a hard error: no cache is written, and the post refuses by name.
  - I also tried the worst case: generate a valid path, edit the op to a level window (49/49), then regenerate. Generate fails with "nothing to face", verify is `ok:false` (stale), and the post is refused with `F1: inputs moved since generation - regenerate before posting`. No file is written.
- The seeded bottom cannot sink below the part's face. The facing plane is Top of Model with offset 0, and the kernel holds the nose ball tangent to that plane. Mutating the offset to -0.5 turns 5 pins red (table below).
- I checked the posted words exactly as emitted (fanuc-lathe, mm). The five axis-crossing passes are `G01 X-1.6 Z50 / Z49.5 / Z49 / Z48.5 / Z48 F0.4`, each with a 0.2 lift (`G00 X-1.6 Z50.2` ...) before the rapid out, and verify is clean.
- Inch document: I set `set_units inch` on the same job. The passes post at `Z1.9685 / 1.9488 / 1.9291 / 1.9094 / 1.8898` (= 50, 49.5, 49, 48.5, 48 mm / 25.4, rounded correctly), and verify is clean. The seed offsets are 0, so they do not depend on the unit.
- Stock shorter than the part (46 vs a 48 part): `add_operation` is refused at creation (`must cut downward`). Nothing is generated.
- The `turning.rs` rework now goes through the real `seed_params` and asserts that no CL point sinks below the part top's tangency. That closes the hole that hid the bug.
- Process: the commit subjects are conventional, the body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1409`, and the decision file is `docs/decisions/1409-face-seed-heights.md`. The PR does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot PNGs, goldens or process files, so no PROCESS_VERSION bump is needed. No `unwrap`/`expect` was added outside tests.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream/main 936172d, no conflicts)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| quick gate `--base upstream/main` (plan below) | green, 1.8 min |
| app lib | 184 passed |
| app: heights_selection 9, plasma_profile 7, probe_op 12, probe_search 3, ribbon 12, shoulder_adaptive 3, sinker_burn 14, sinker_side 6, tool_law 4, trochoid_op 5, turning 6, turning_face_seed 3, wire_contour 8 | all pass |
| ui lib (CWD crates/ui) | 666 passed, 5 ignored |
| ui: boundary 3, boundary_picks 6, theme_files 14 | all pass |
| extra: drill_prior 12, lathe_post 7, lathe_post_inch 6, mcp_verify 3, project_roundtrip 73, turning_face_approach 3, turning_stock_approach 3 | all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets` | no warnings in app or ui |

Clippy note: `-D warnings` stops in **camcraft-geometry**, which this PR does not touch. The lint is `needless_range_loop` at `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:481`, `:1205` and `:1486`. It comes from the newer clippy (1.100) on this machine and is already on main, so it is not this PR's.

### Mutation check (each mutation applied, the suites run, then restored)
| Mutation | Red |
|---|---|
| M1: seed back to fold `c.top`/`c.bottom` | 3/3 turning_face_seed, `turning::the_facing_seed_faces_the_bar`, ui quick-add pin |
| M2: `depth_sane` Facing re-tightened to `t > b` | `a_seeded_facing_on_a_part_at_length_reports_nothing_to_face` |
| **M3: `depth_sane` Facing loosened to always pass (top below plane accepted)** | **nothing.** I ran app lib and every `turning*`, `lathe*`, `heights*` and `mcp*` app suite: all green |
| M4: seed facing plane at Top of Model - 0.5 (below the part face) | 3/3 turning_face_seed, `the_facing_seed_faces_the_bar`, ui pin |
| M5: seed top = Top of Model (no allowance) | 2 turning_face_seed, `the_facing_seed_faces_the_bar`, ui pin |
| M6 (kernel, unchanged here): `hi <= s_face` -> `hi < s_face` | at-length pin, `drill_prior::a_finished_part_with_no_stock_allowance_has_nothing_to_face`, 2 motion `turning_face` tests |

With M3 applied, an inverted edit (top 47 / plane 48) is accepted and generate then refuses it as "nothing to face". So the kernel is a real backstop and no G-code escapes. But the door claim the PR states ("A top below the plane is still refused at creation") is not pinned.

### Requested before merge
1. **Pin the inverted-window refusal for Facing** (`crates/app/tests/turning_face_seed.rs`). Add a test that creates the seeded `F1`, then calls `edit_operation` with `top_z` Fixed 47 and `bottom_z` Fixed 48 and asserts the refusal contains `must cut downward`. Add the epsilon case too, `top_z` 48 and `bottom_z` 48 + 1e-9. Today both refuse (I checked), but loosening the new `t >= b` arm turns nothing red. A direct `operation::depth_sane` assertion beside the existing ones in `crates/app/tests/heights.rs` would do as well.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` was already 2606 lines and is now 2614. That is far past the ~400-line rule. It is not this PR's to split, but it is worth a follow-up.
- When the stock is shorter than the part, the refusal reads "a Facing operation must cut downward: its top height resolves below its bottom height". That is true, but a user would understand "the stock's top stands below the part's top - nothing to face" better. This could be a P7 follow-up.
- The first pass at Z50 runs tangent to the stock top and so cuts air. This is the kernel's existing ladder law (anchored on the facing plane) and matches the issue's expected output. It is mentioned only for completeness.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
